2026-12-15.weatherAlert: December evenings in Tokyo are cold (often near freezing). The Omoide Yokocho outdoor stalls can be frigid.
tips: Layer up for evening alley walks; the cold wind tunnels under the train tracks.
Hit the Limousine Bus desk before immigration if buying tickets to avoid the post-baggage claim queue.

2026-12-16.weatherAlert: High rain risk for an outdoor-heavy day. Meiji Shrine walk, Cat Street, and Blue Cave illumination are fully exposed.

suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Miyashita Park covered rooftop + Parco + Tower Records
suggestedSwap.reason: The Blue Cave illumination is an outdoor walk of ~600k LEDs toward Yoyogi that is miserable in December rain; the covered Miyashita Park and Parco complex keeps the squad dry and entertained.

tips: Check the Shibuya Sky weather camera before heading up; clouds will ruin the sunset slot.
If the rain holds off, grab the free Tokyo Metropolitan Gov't Building night view instead of paying for Shibuya Sky.

2026-12-17.weatherAlert: Rain risk continues. Senso-ji and Nakamise are fine under cover, but Ueno Ameyoko and Skytree queues are exposed.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Ueno Ameyoko market under the tracks
suggestedSwap.reason: Ameyoko is largely exposed to the elements, while the Tokyo National Museum is an indoor world-class highlight perfectly situated between Asakusa and Akihabara on the same line.

tips: Skytree has covered waiting, but the outdoor observation decks are brutal in winter wind; check conditions before paying for the top.
Kamiya Bar in Asakusa is a perfect indoor warm-up with Denki Bran before heading south.
teamLab Planets requires rolling up pants and wading through water; December water is cold, so they provide warm water and shorts, but prepare mentally.
Depachika raids are an ideal rainy-day activity since they are entirely underground/indoor.

2026-12-19.weatherAlert: Coastal Kamakura and Enoshima are highly exposed to cold December winds and rain. The Enoden tram ride can be delayed in severe weather.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Enoshima island — climb to the Sea Candle
suggestedSwap.reason: Climbing Enoshima in cold, wet, and windy December weather is exhausting; Enospa offers a warm soak with the same bay and potential Fuji view.

tips: The Fuji-over-Sagami-Bay sunset requires clear skies; if it's overcast at 15:00, pivot to the Hokokuji bamboo temple in Kamakura instead.
Sit on the right side of the Enoden train heading west for the best coastal views.
Ghibli Museum tickets are strictly timed; arrive exactly at your slot, not early, as they rarely let you in ahead of schedule.
Use the Airbnb washer during the wagyu dinner so everyone packs clean clothes for Kyoto.
Sit on the RIGHT side of the Nozomi shinkansen for the Mt. Fuji view around minute 40 out of Tokyo.
Pontocho Alley restaurants are notoriously narrow; confirm the booking accommodates all 8 together or split into two adjacent tables.

2026-12-22.weatherAlert: Fushimi Inari at dawn in December is freezing. The stone steps are hazardous if wet from overnight rain.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Kiyomizu-dera — the wooden stage over the valley
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Sanjusangendo — 1,001 golden Kannon statues in a 120m hall
suggestedSwap.reason: Kiyomizu-dera's iconic wooden stage offers no cover from rain; Sanjusangendo is an indoor, jaw-dropping, and criminally underrated alternative just a short bus ride away.

tips: Hand warmers (kairo) are sold at every konbini for ~¥100; buy a pack before the dawn hike at Fushimi Inari.
Funaoka Onsen's electric bath is an experience, but don't overstay—3 seconds is enough for first-timers.

2026-12-23.weatherAlert: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove is highly susceptible to rain, which ruins the photographic atmosphere and makes the paths slick.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove before the buses exist
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: SNOW PROTOCOL: Kinkaku-ji at opening (gold + snow = Japan's rarest photo)
suggestedSwap.reason: If Kyoto wakes up white, the Bamboo Grove under snow is beautiful but the Golden Pavilion reflected in the snow is Japan's rarest and most iconic photo opportunity, overriding the standard itinerary.

tips: Wakakusa-yama is closed for the winter (since Dec 13), so do not attempt the climb even if the weather looks perfect.
Nara deer can be aggressive if they see food; buy the deer crackers but finish feeding them completely before entering the temple grounds.

2026-12-24.crowdAlert: KFC Christmas buckets sell out fast on December 24th. Pre-ordering is usually required for locals, so find a location early and be prepared to wait in line or pivot to convenience store fried chicken.
tips: Nintendo Museum lottery tickets are locked months ago; if the squad lost, embrace Uji's matcha and Byodo-in fully rather than dwelling on the L.
Dotonbori on Christmas Eve will be packed with couples; walk single-file across Ebisubashi to avoid getting split.

2026-12-25.crowdAlert: USJ on Christmas Day will be at peak capacity. Super Nintendo World timed entry passes sell out in minutes if not on an Express Pass.
tips: Rope-drop the park 45 minutes before official opening to secure the app timed-entry for Mario Kart if you lack Express Passes.
Single-rider lines for Forbidden Journey and Mario Kart cut 60% off wait times if the group is okay riding separately.

2026-12-26.weatherAlert: Miyajima island is fully exposed to cold Inland Sea winds. The floating torii is best at high tide, which in winter often coincides with the coldest part of the afternoon.
tips: Check the Miyajima tide times; if low tide is at 14:30, the torii will be beached and walking out to it is muddy and cold rather than floating.
The Peace Memorial Museum hits heavy; it's okay to take a quiet walk through Shukkei-en garden afterward to decompress before the ferry.

2026-12-27.weatherAlert: The Midosuji Illumination is a 4km outdoor walk. December nights are freezing, and wind tunnels down the long boulevard.
tips: 551 Horai butaman (pork buns) sell out nightly; grab a 4-pack at Namba station BEFORE the crab dinner for the ultimate midnight Airbnb snack.
Split squads for Den Den Town and Amerikamura, but set a hard regroup time at Umeda Sky Building to catch the sunset.
Himeji Castle involves steep, cold climbs in December; wear shoes with good grip as the wooden steps can be slick.
Do a tax-free paperwork check tonight: ensure all receipts are stapled in passports and purchases are accessible for customs on exit.
Sit on the LEFT side of the eastbound Nozomi shinkansen for the final Mt. Fuji encore view.
Zero out your Suica cards by buying last-minute snacks or gachapon; convenience stores allow split payments to drain the exact remaining balance.

globalTips: The USD/JPY rate is highly favorable (~161 JPY to 1 USD). Avoid exchanging cash at airports; withdraw directly from 7-Eleven ATMs for the best rates and carry cash, as many small izakayas and temples are cash-only.

December in Japan is cold and dry, but rain can ruin outdoor-heavy days (especially in Kyoto and Kamakura). Always carry a compact umbrella and buy 'kairo' (hand warmers) from konbinis for dawn temple visits.

For a group of 8, always make dinner reservations as far in advance as possible. Walk-ins at popular izakayas and shabu-shabu spots are nearly impossible for large groups, and you'll often need to split into two tables anyway.
